zebralogic.title: PreserveExactCase
zebralogic.principle: Copy every attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem statement, preserving case and punctuation; without this, the model may output values with incorrect capitalization, causing a mismatch with the reference solution.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever an attribute value is taken from the problem description or clues and placed into the solution grid.
zebralogic.example: Outputting "Mar" instead of the required "mar" for the month March.

zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that state "X is directly left of Y" as X's house number = Y's house number − 1; without this, the model may treat the relationship as a non‑adjacent left‑of, violating the exact adjacency requirement.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrase "directly left of" (or equivalent wording).
zebralogic.example: Placing X two houses left of Y instead of immediately left.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: Treat clues that say "X is somewhere to the left of Y" as a strict ordering constraint X < Y, without requiring adjacency; missing this leads to ignoring the required ordering.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a left‑of relationship without the word "directly".
zebralogic.example: Allowing X to be placed to the right of Y despite a "somewhere left of" clue.

zebralogic.title: AdjacencyWithoutOrientation
zebralogic.principle: Interpret clues that say "X and Y are next to each other" as |X − Y| = 1, with no implied left/right orientation; without this, the model may incorrectly enforce a direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses "next to each other", "adjacent", or similar phrasing without specifying left or right.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X must be left of Y when the clue only requires them to be adjacent.

zebralogic.title: ExactDistance
zebralogic.principle: For clues stating "There are N houses between X and Y", enforce |X − Y| = N + 1; without this, the model may mis‑interpret the distance.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses separating two entities.
zebralogic.example: Placing X and Y with only one house between them when the clue says there are two houses between them.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attributes refer to the same entity, treat them as a combined attribute (e.g., "the person with a master's degree is the person whose birthday is in March"); without this, the model may assign the linked attributes to different houses.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue directly links two attribute values to the same person.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the master degree to one house and the March birthday to a different house.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, assign that attribute to that house immediately; without this, the model may leave the placement ambiguous or violate the clue.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a concrete house number (e.g., "Alice is in the third house").
zebralogic.example: Leaving Alice unassigned to house 3 despite the explicit clue.

zebralogic.title: ExclusionConstraints
zebralogic.principle: Respect clues that forbid an attribute from a specific house (e.g., "X is not in house 4") by eliminating that possibility; without this, the model may place the attribute incorrectly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains a negation about a house position.
zebralogic.example: Placing Eric in house 2 despite a clue that he is not in house 2.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceSubstitutionBeforeOrderingAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: Before applying ordering or adjacency constraints, replace any attribute reference with the concrete entity established by equivalence linking; without this, ordering may be applied to the wrong placeholder.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After processing equivalence links and before handling left‑of, right‑of, adjacency, or distance clues.
zebralogic.example: Applying "X left of Y" using the original attribute name instead of the already‑linked concrete person.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Ensure the final JSON output is syntactically valid: all arrays and objects are properly closed with matching brackets, commas are placed correctly, and required top‑level keys are present; without this, the verifier will reject the answer even if the logical solution is correct.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After constructing the solution JSON and before emitting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Outputting JSON that ends with "... \"rows\":[[...], [...]]}"—missing the final closing bracket for the rows array—resulting in malformed JSON.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model rewrites attribute strings and unintentionally changes their case or punctuation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute values verbatim from the problem statement; never alter case or spelling.

zebralogic.description: Capitalization mismatch for phone model values
zebralogic.why_it_happens: Similar to other attributes, the model may normalize or capitalize phone model names incorrectly.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat phone model strings as immutable literals and copy them exactly.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may drop a clue during reasoning or fail to propagate its implication to the assignment stage.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit list of all constraints and verify after each inference that no clue has been discarded.

zebralogic.description: Missing required top‑level keys in output JSON
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the solution grid and forgets to wrap it in the expected JSON envelope.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Always construct the final answer as a JSON object with the prescribed top‑level keys before printing.

zebralogic.description: Malformed JSON due to missing closing brackets
zebralogic.why_it_happens: When concatenating strings to build nested JSON arrays, the model can lose track of opening brackets, especially for the outer "rows" array.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After building the JSON string, run a quick syntactic check (e.g., try parsing it) or manually count opening and closing brackets to ensure they match before output.
